root_idea.summary: The evidence presents two related semantic strands: cutting or severing, from which wounding and reviling are developed; and a strand of length and extension associated with a rope, a means of access, and a route.
root_idea.development: Classical analysis treats reviling as developed from cutting or severance, while the rope-and-route branch may represent a distinct root development based on length and extension.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed under the singular nominal citation form.

senses.definition: To revile, insult, vilify, or speak abusively against someone.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, the prohibition against reviling those worshipped besides God is linked to the danger that they will respond by reviling God; the imperfect forms represent the ongoing or prospective action.

senses.definition: A rope or cord, especially one used for climbing, descending, or gaining access.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic literal image is a rope extended upward; the plural may refer to ropes or means of ascent.

senses.definition: A means, avenue, or route by which one reaches or attains something; a way or course of access.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, the word can denote a means of access or an avenue followed toward an objective, including ways or routes associated with ascent to the heavens.

senses.definition: A tie or connection, especially a bond of relationship by marriage; a bond or attachment between people.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural expression, the severing of such ties is associated with the dissolution of bonds and affections.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut; by extension, to wound, hock, hamstring, or otherwise sever the flesh of someone or an animal.
To penetrate the anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare anatomical usage marked as figurative or transferred in the lexical source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, appoint, or prepare a means or cause; to cause or occasion something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be followed by لِـ to indicate preparing a means for an affair or objective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To revile, reproach, or defame one another; to exchange abusive speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The corresponding verbal noun denotes mutual reviling between two parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a means or cause, or to use something as a means of access or attainment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may be used in a quasi-passive sense for something becoming causally effective, or with بِهِ إِلَى to express using something as a means to an end.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To engage in trade or trafficking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later usage explained as treating commerce as a means of obtaining subsistence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or wound one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal Form VI usage; the plural subject may be more than two people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To revile, vilify, reproach, or defame one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal usage; the related noun may denote abusive speech exchanged between the parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To invite, attract, or expose someone to reviling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe provoking retaliatory abuse against another person, especially a parent or protector.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become caused or prepared for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred causative usage describing an affair or event as becoming arranged or occasioned for a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sever one's ties of relationship through unkind treatment of one's kindred.
To go at a gentle or easy pace.
To emit or detect a foul smell.
To discharge urine; to make water flow.
For water to run or flow.
A person who reviles much, or one who mutually reviles another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote either a habitual or intense reviler or a party in mutual abuse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covering or elongated piece of cloth, including a veil, head-covering, turban, or thin cloth strip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usages are connected with a long or extended piece of textile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A euphemistic anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A space or period of time, especially a prolonged interval.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of a period of several days characterized by weather or other prevailing conditions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disgrace, shame, or thing that occasions someone being reviled.
A person whom people revile much.
A cause, occasion, reason, or motive by which something comes about.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the broader abstract causal usage, distinct from the Quranic noun senses of a physical rope, route, or interpersonal tie.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prosodic unit consisting either of a consonant with a following quiescent letter or of two successive movent letters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Technical terminology in Arabic prosody; the light and heavy types are distinguished by their structure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who reviles people, or one who is habitually reviled.
Causative; relating to a cause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Technical relational adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Causality or the relation of cause and effect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Technical abstract noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hair of a horse's forelock, tail, or mane; also a lock or plait of hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may denote pendent locks or plaits of hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A streak or strip of blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually encountered in the plural expression for streaks of blood upon someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place abounding in trees of the ʿiḍāh kind.
A sword that cuts sharply, especially one that cuts the hock tendons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet of the sword based on its cutting force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who reviles much or frequently; a great reviler.
The index finger, the finger between the thumb and middle finger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is associated with pointing during reviling; it is also called the finger raised in affirming God's unity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert or far-extending tract of barren land, especially one lacking water, herbage, or settlement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may be used adjectivally of a level or otherwise extensive desolate land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree from which arrows or camel saddles are made.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical identification also associated with a dialectal or variant tree name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Christian festival, identified with Palm Sunday or the days of the palms.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional cultural designation rather than a general plural of the desert noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A form or piece of reviling speech used by people against one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may denote abusive expressions exchanged between parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beauties or attractive features of the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much reviled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive participial usage derived from the reviling sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Goodly or excellent, especially as an admiring epithet for camels, horses, or wild asses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is based on a non-literal admiring invocation rather than an intended curse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Caused or occasioned; an effect or result arising from something else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction مُسَبَّبٌ عَنْ to express an effect arising from a cause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who reviles much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active participial usage derived from the reviling sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who makes or prepares a means or cause; a causer or occasioner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used as an epithet of God, the maker or disposer of causes and means.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who mutually reviles another; a participant in reciprocal abuse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may function as an active or passive participle in the cited usage.
